newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish markets calm, hesitant after ERM link.
newsitem.headline: Finnish markets calm, hesitant after ERM link.

text.p: The Finnish markka was steady, bonds firmed slightly but forestry stocks eased in broadly hesitant early Monday trade after the markka was linked to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) at the weekend.

The markka opened at 2.9860 bid per German mark, unchanged from its Friday close in Helsinki. At 1125/0825 GMT, it traded fractionally weaker at 2.9880/10 per mark with little change against other currencies.

The central parity rate for the markka's peg to Europe's currency stability mechanism was 3.04 per German mark with 15 percent fluctuation bands either way, but dealers said a notional ceiling on 2.25 percent strengthening would be 2.9724.
On Sunday analysts had seen pressure for the currency to firm further as corporates seek to repatriate foreign earnings.
"We went to higher (DEM/FIM) levels in Singapore so (the upside) got tested," said Esko Torsti, head of Enskilda market advisory here.
"It clearly showed there is no reason for the markka to soften for a while although its central parity rate is higher," he added.
"We were working last night and clients called us all the time and put in orders (at high DEM/FIM levels)," said one dealer.
But Torsti noted that the markka was not likely to firm very dramatically either since the central bank would probably intervene to keep it steady.
Dealers spoke of rumours of early intervention at 2.9850 per mark, but there was broad uncertainty about their validity.
"We have heard rumours but are not sure whether they are true of not," one dealer said.

Stocks were steady to easier with forestries getting off to a wobbly start amid some concern for the Finnish industry's competitive prospects, as some voiced fears if the markka pegged to ERM but Sweden stayed out.
The HEX index was off around 0.14 percent at 2,181.65 with the forestries' sub-index shedding 1.6 percent. UPM-Kymmene fell three percent at its first trade but recovered to slightly weaker levels.

"Many players had decided to sell forestries if Finland joins the ERM and Sweden stays out," one broker said; but added that weakness was likely to be a temporary knee-jerk reaction with bargain-hunters set to sniff out opportunities.

Quiet early selling took bond yields off their pre-opening best but yields were still clearly below last Friday, with the 2006 bond yielding 41 basis points over its German equivalent, against 48 basis points at Friday's close.
The yield spread over Bunds was seen shrinking to around 40 basis points near-term from 48 basis points on Friday, and bond dealers said in the long term it could shrink further.
"Nothing has really happened here yet, some sellers came in (at the early levels) but now there are some bids around too and we have stabilised for the time being," one trader said.
"Today will probably be more volatile than recent weeks as we will look for a new level," said another.
